data.name: Dheerandra
data.gender_notes: Dheerandra is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Dheerandra is derived from the Sanskrit words ‘dheera’ meaning fearless and ‘andra’ meaning man. This name is attributed to several mythological figures in Hinduism, who displayed immense courage and bravery. The name Dheerandra carries the meaning “Fearless, Valiant” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dheerandra usually hope their child will grow to embody fearless, valiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dheerandra total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

It exemplifies the valor and strength associated with numerous Hindu deities and heroes. Numerous Hindu rulers and warriors have been named Dheerandra, inspiring their armies and subjects with their fearless spirit. This powerful name continues to be popular among Hindus, a testament to the enduring influence of their rich cultural heritage.

It represents an individual's inner strength and fearlessness, inspiring them to face challenges boldly and bravely. The name is believed to ward off negative energies, granting the bearer a protective shield of courage and resilience. Additionally, it is said to symbolize moral fortitude, encouraging individuals to stand firm in their values and convictions, even in the face of adversity.

historical_references.reference:
Dheerandra was a famous Jain monk and philosopher from the 12th century. He is considered one of the greatest scholars of Jainism and is known for his commentaries on various Jain texts. He was a disciple of Hemachandra, the founder of the Digambara Terapanth sect of Jainism.
Time Period: 1178 - 1271 AD
Context: Jainism, Philosophy, Scholarship

Dheerandra was also a renowned poet and wrote numerous works in Sanskrit, Prakrit and Apabhramsha languages. His works include commentaries on the Agama texts, collections of stories and hymns, and a treatise on the nature of the self. He is considered the last great Jain poet in Kannada literature.
Time Period: 12th - 13th century AD
Context: Jainism, Literature, Poetry
